title: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
summary: Proposes a purely peer-to-peer electronic cash system that prevents double-spending with a proof-of-work chain of timestamped blocks, removing the need for a trusted third party.

title: Ethereum Whitepaper: A Next-Generation Smart Contract and Decentralized Application Platform
summary: Describes a blockchain with a built-in Turing-complete programming language so anyone can write smart contracts and decentralized applications with their own rules for ownership, transaction formats and state transitions.

title: Ethereum: A Secure Decentralised Generalised Transaction Ledger (Yellow Paper)
summary: The formal specification of the Ethereum protocol, defining the state-transition function, the Ethereum Virtual Machine, gas and block validation rules.

title: Solana: A New Architecture for a High Performance Blockchain
summary: Introduces Proof of History, a verifiable sequence of SHA-256 hashes that timestamps events, combined with a proof-of-stake consensus to reach high throughput without waiting for network-wide clock agreement.

title: Ouroboros: A Provably Secure Proof-of-Stake Blockchain Protocol
authors: Aggelos Kiayias, Alexander Russell, Bernardo David, Roman Oliynykov
summary: The proof-of-stake protocol behind Cardano, the first with rigorous security guarantees comparable to Bitcoin's, using a provably secure coin-flipping protocol to elect slot leaders.

title: Polkadot: Vision for a Heterogeneous Multi-Chain Framework
summary: Proposes a scalable heterogeneous multi-chain in which a relay chain provides pooled security and consensus for many parachains that can pass messages to one another.

title: Overview of Polkadot and its Design Considerations
authors: Jeff Burdges, Alfonso Cevallos, Peter Czaban, Rob Habermeier, et al. (Web3 Foundation)
summary: A later technical overview of the Polkadot design: shared security for parachains, the BABE and GRANDPA consensus components, NPoS validator selection and cross-chain messaging.

title: Cosmos: A Network of Distributed Ledgers
summary: Proposes a network of independent parallel blockchains (zones) secured by Tendermint BFT consensus and connected through a Hub using inter-blockchain communication.

title: The Latest Gossip on BFT Consensus
authors: Ethan Buchman, Jae Kwon, Zarko Milosevic
summary: Presents the Tendermint consensus algorithm, a Byzantine fault-tolerant protocol for blockchains that relies on gossip communication and a simple termination mechanism.

title: Scalable and Probabilistic Leaderless BFT Consensus through Metastability
authors: Team Rocket, Maofan Yin, Kevin Sekniqi, Robbert van Renesse, Emin Gün Sirer
summary: Introduces the Snow family of consensus protocols (Slush, Snowflake, Snowball, Avalanche), which use repeated random subsampling of validators to reach metastable agreement.

title: Avalanche Platform Whitepaper
authors: Kevin Sekniqi, Daniel Laine, Stephen Buttolph, Emin Gün Sirer
summary: Describes the Avalanche platform architecture: subnets, the primary network's chains, the AVAX token and its governance mechanism.

title: ALGORAND
summary: Presents a public ledger that uses cryptographic sortition and a fast Byzantine agreement protocol to confirm transactions with tiny forking probability and minimal computation.

title: Tezos: A Self-Amending Crypto-Ledger
summary: Describes a blockchain that can amend its own protocol through on-chain stakeholder voting, avoiding hard forks, with proof-of-stake consensus.

title: The Open Network
authors: Based on the work of Dr. Nikolai Durov
summary: Describes TON's scalable multi-blockchain architecture with a masterchain, workchains and dynamically split shardchains, plus TON networking, storage, DNS and payments. Updated 2021 version of the 2017 Telegram Open Network paper.

title: TRON: Advanced Decentralized Blockchain Platform (Whitepaper v2.0)
summary: Describes TRON's three-layer architecture, delegated proof-of-stake consensus with Super Representatives, the TRON Virtual Machine and token standards.

title: Hedera: A Public Hashgraph Network & Governing Council (v2.1)
authors: Leemon Baird, Mance Harmon, Paul Madsen
summary: Describes the Hedera public network built on hashgraph consensus, its services, its council-based governance and the economics of the HBAR coin.

title: The Swirlds Hashgraph Consensus Algorithm: Fair, Fast, Byzantine Fault Tolerance
summary: Introduces hashgraph, an asynchronous BFT consensus that uses 'gossip about gossip' and virtual voting to agree on transaction order without sending votes.

title: Nightshade: Near Protocol Sharding Design 2.0
authors: Alex Skidanov, Illia Polosukhin, Bowen Wang
summary: NEAR's sharding design, in which every block holds chunks produced by each shard; the 2.0 version adds stateless validation and updated data-availability handling.

title: The Sui Smart Contracts Platform
summary: Describes Sui, a smart-contract platform built around an object-centric data model and the Move language, where simple transactions on owned objects can bypass full consensus.

title: The Aptos Blockchain: Safe, Scalable, and Upgradeable Web3 Infrastructure
summary: Presents Aptos, a Move-based layer 1 with BFT consensus, pipelined and parallel transaction execution (Block-STM) and built-in upgradeability.

title: The Internet Computer for Geeks (v1.4)
summary: Technical description of the Internet Computer: subnets of nodes running canister smart contracts, chain-key cryptography and the Network Nervous System governance.

title: The Ripple Protocol Consensus Algorithm
authors: David Schwartz, Noah Youngs, Arthur Britto
summary: Describes the Ripple consensus algorithm, in which nodes reach agreement using collectively trusted subnetworks (Unique Node Lists) instead of mining.

title: Analysis of the XRP Ledger Consensus Protocol
summary: A detailed analysis of the XRP Ledger consensus protocol's safety and liveness, with conditions on overlap between nodes' trusted lists.

title: The Stellar Consensus Protocol: A Federated Model for Internet-level Consensus
summary: Introduces federated Byzantine agreement, where each node chooses its own quorum slices, enabling open membership with low latency and flexible trust.

title: PHANTOM and GHOSTDAG: A Scalable Generalization of Nakamoto Consensus
authors: Yonatan Sompolinsky, Shai Wyborski, Aviv Zohar
summary: Generalizes Nakamoto consensus to a block DAG, ordering blocks via a greedy 'GHOSTDAG' algorithm so that throughput can grow without hurting security; the basis of Kaspa.

title: The Zilliqa Technical Whitepaper
summary: Describes a blockchain that scales throughput through network and transaction sharding, using PBFT consensus within shards.

title: EOS.IO Technical White Paper v2
summary: Describes the EOS.IO software: delegated proof-of-stake with elected block producers, a resource model without per-transaction fees, and parallel-friendly smart contracts.

title: Mina: Decentralized Cryptocurrency at Scale
authors: Joseph Bonneau, Izaak Meckler, Vanishree Rao, Evan Shapiro
summary: Presents a succinct blockchain whose entire state is verified by a constant-size recursive zk-SNARK, so any device can fully verify the chain.

title: MonadBFT: Fast, Responsive, Fork-Resistant Streamlined Consensus
authors: Mohammad Mussadiq Jalalzai, Kushal Babel, Jovan Komatovic, Tobias Klenze, Sourav Das, et al.
summary: Monad's HotStuff-family BFT consensus with linear message complexity in the common case, optimistic responsiveness and resistance to tail-forking.

title: Casper the Friendly Finality Gadget
summary: Introduces Casper, a proof-of-stake finality system that overlays an existing proposal mechanism and provides accountable safety and plausible liveness.

title: Combining GHOST and Casper (Gasper)
authors: Vitalik Buterin, Diego Hernandez, Thor Kamphefner, Khiem Pham, Zhi Qiao, Danny Ryan, et al.
summary: Specifies Gasper, the proof-of-stake consensus of Ethereum's Beacon Chain, combining Casper FFG finality with the LMD GHOST fork-choice rule.

title: HotStuff: BFT Consensus in the Lens of Blockchain
authors: Maofan Yin, Dahlia Malkhi, Michael K. Reiter, Guy Golan Gueta, Ittai Abraham
summary: A leader-based BFT replication protocol with linear view change and optimistic responsiveness; its design shaped consensus in Diem, Aptos and many newer chains.

title: The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments
summary: Proposes a network of bidirectional micropayment channels with hashed timelock contracts so Bitcoin payments can be made off-chain instantly and routed across many hops.

title: Plasma: Scalable Autonomous Smart Contracts
summary: Proposes a framework of child blockchains anchored to Ethereum with fraud proofs and exits, enabling scalable computation enforced by the root chain.

title: Arbitrum: Scalable, Private Smart Contracts
authors: Harry Kalodner, Steven Goldfeder, Xiaoqi Chen, S. Matthew Weinberg, Edward W. Felten
summary: USENIX Security 2018 paper introducing Arbitrum, where managers execute contracts off-chain and disputes are resolved on-chain by an efficient bisection protocol.

title: Arbitrum Nitro: A Second-Generation Optimistic Rollup
authors: Lee Bousfield, Rachel Bousfield, Chris Buckland, Ben Burgess, Joshua Colvin, Edward W. Felten, Steven Goldfeder, Harry Kalodner, et al.
summary: Describes Nitro, Arbitrum's optimistic rollup design that compiles Geth to WebAssembly for fraud proofs and uses interactive dispute resolution.

title: OP Stack Specification
summary: The official specification of the OP Stack optimistic rollup: derivation, batch submission, bridging and the Cannon fault-proof system. Optimism has no classic whitepaper; this is its canonical technical document.

title: ZKsync: The Elastic Network Endgame
summary: ZKsync's paper on its Elastic Network, a set of interoperable ZK chains built with the open-source ZK Stack and sharing liquidity and trustless bridging.

title: Matic Network Whitepaper
summary: The original Matic Network whitepaper describing a proof-of-stake sidechain and Plasma framework for scaling Ethereum, the forerunner of Polygon PoS.

title: POL Token White Paper (MiCA)
summary: Polygon's EU MiCA-format white paper (notified Dec 2025) for POL, the gas and staking token of the Polygon PoS network and the upgrade of MATIC.

title: LazyLedger: A Distributed Data Availability Ledger With Client-Side Smart Contracts
summary: Proposes a blockchain that only orders and guarantees availability of data, with data-availability sampling and client-side execution; the design that became Celestia.

title: EigenLayer: The Restaking Collective
summary: Proposes restaking, letting Ethereum stakers opt in to extra slashing conditions so their staked ETH can secure new actively validated services such as DA layers, oracles and bridges.

title: EIGEN: The Universal Intersubjective Work Token
summary: Introduces the EIGEN token as a work token for intersubjective faults, which can be resolved by social consensus via token forking.

title: EIP-4844: Shard Blob Transactions (Proto-Danksharding)
authors: Vitalik Buterin, Dankrad Feist, Diederik Loerwald, George Kadianakis, Matt Garnett, Mofi Taiwo, Ansgar Dietrichs
summary: Introduces blob-carrying transactions that give rollups cheap, temporary data space on Ethereum, a first step toward full danksharding.

title: Uniswap v2 Core
authors: Hayden Adams, Noah Zinsmeister, Dan Robinson
summary: Describes Uniswap v2's constant-product AMM, adding arbitrary ERC-20 pairs, a manipulation-resistant price oracle and flash swaps.

title: Uniswap v3 Core
authors: Hayden Adams, Noah Zinsmeister, Moody Salem, River Keefer, Dan Robinson
summary: Introduces concentrated liquidity, letting LPs provide capital within custom price ranges, plus multiple fee tiers and improved oracles.

title: Uniswap v4 Core
authors: Hayden Adams, Moody Salem, Noah Zinsmeister, Sara Reynolds, Austin Adams, Will Pote, Mark Toda, Alice Henshaw, Emily Williams, Dan Robinson
summary: Describes v4's hooks for customizing pools, a singleton contract holding all pools, flash accounting and native ETH support.

title: UniswapX
authors: Hayden Adams, Noah Zinsmeister, Mark Toda, Emily Williams, Xin Wan, Matteo Leibowitz, Will Pote, Allen Lin, Eric Zhong, Zhiyuan Sun, Riley Campbell, Alex Karys, Dan Robinson
summary: An auction-based, intent-style trading protocol where fillers compete to execute signed orders across liquidity sources, with gas-free swaps and MEV protection.

title: Aave Protocol Whitepaper v1.0
summary: Describes Aave's decentralized lending pools with interest-bearing aTokens, variable and stable rates, and flash loans.

title: Aave Protocol V2 Whitepaper
summary: Aave V2 adds debt tokenization, credit delegation, collateral swaps, repay-with-collateral and gas optimizations.

title: Aave V3 Technical Paper
summary: Aave V3 introduces Portals for cross-chain liquidity, High Efficiency (eMode), Isolation Mode, supply and borrow caps, and gas savings.

title: Compound: The Money Market Protocol
summary: Describes money markets on Ethereum with algorithmically set interest rates based on supply and demand, and cTokens representing supplied balances.

title: StableSwap: Efficient Mechanism for Stablecoin Liquidity
summary: Introduces the StableSwap invariant, a blend of constant-sum and constant-product curves that gives low slippage for assets that should trade near parity.

title: Automatic Market-Making with Dynamic Peg
summary: Curve v2 (CryptoSwap): concentrates liquidity around an internal oracle price that re-pegs when profitable, for volatile asset pairs.

title: Balancer: A Non-Custodial Portfolio Manager, Liquidity Provider, and Price Sensor
summary: Generalizes the constant-product AMM to weighted pools of up to eight tokens that self-rebalance as traders arbitrage them.

title: THORChain: A Decentralised Liquidity Network
summary: Describes a cross-chain liquidity network where nodes custody native assets in threshold-signature vaults and continuous liquidity pools swap them against RUNE.

title: Lido: Ethereum Liquid Staking
summary: Proposes a liquid staking protocol where users deposit ETH, receive stETH that tracks their staked balance, and stake is delegated to curated node operators.

title: Hyperliquid Docs: HyperBFT, HyperCore and HyperEVM
summary: Hyperliquid has no standalone whitepaper; its official docs describe an L1 running HyperBFT consensus with an on-chain order-book exchange (HyperCore) and HyperEVM.

title: The Dai Stablecoin System
summary: Describes Dai, a decentralized stablecoin soft-pegged to the US dollar and backed by over-collateralized debt positions, with MKR as the governance token.

title: Tether: Fiat Currencies on the Bitcoin Blockchain
summary: Proposes fiat-pegged tokens issued on Bitcoin's Omni Layer and backed one-to-one by reserves. Tether now presents it for historical interest only.

title: Ethena Docs: USDe Synthetic Dollar
summary: Ethena publishes docs rather than a whitepaper; they describe USDe, a synthetic dollar backed by crypto collateral and delta-neutral short perpetual hedges.

title: ChainLink: A Decentralized Oracle Network
authors: Steve Ellis, Ari Juels, Sergey Nazarov
summary: Proposes a decentralized network of oracles that supply external data to smart contracts, with reputation and aggregation to resist faulty nodes.

title: Chainlink 2.0: Next Steps in the Evolution of Decentralized Oracle Networks
authors: Lorenz Breidenbach, Christian Cachin, Alex Coventry, Steve Ellis, Ari Juels, Andrew Miller, Sergey Nazarov, et al.
summary: Expands Chainlink into decentralized oracle networks offering hybrid smart contracts, off-chain computation, fair sequencing and super-linear staking.

title: Pyth Network: A First-Party Financial Oracle (v2.0)
summary: Describes Pyth's first-party price feeds from trading firms and exchanges, aggregated on Pythnet and delivered cross-chain with a pull-oracle model.

title: The Graph: A Decentralized Query Protocol for Blockchains
authors: Yaniv Tal, Brandon Ramirez, Jannis Pohlmann
summary: Proposes a decentralized protocol for indexing and querying blockchain data via subgraphs and GraphQL, served by staked indexing nodes.

title: Wormhole: Generic Message Passing (Design Document 0001)
summary: Wormhole's founding design document: a guardian network observes messages on one chain and signs Verified Action Approvals that any other chain can verify.

title: IPFS: Content Addressed, Versioned, P2P File System
summary: Proposes a peer-to-peer distributed file system that combines a DHT, BitTorrent-style exchange and a Git-like Merkle DAG for content-addressed storage.

title: Filecoin: A Decentralized Storage Network
summary: Describes a storage marketplace where miners earn FIL by storing and serving data, verified through Proof-of-Replication and Proof-of-Spacetime.

title: Arweave: A Protocol for Economically Sustainable Information Permanence (Yellow Paper)
authors: Sam Williams, Viktor Diordiiev, India Raybould, Lev Berman, Ivan Uemlianin
summary: Describes a blockweave for permanent data storage, with a storage endowment funding long-term replication and proof-of-access mining.

title: Sia: Simple Decentralized Storage
summary: Proposes a decentralized storage platform where file contracts on a blockchain pay hosts who prove they still store the data.

title: Storj: A Decentralized Cloud Storage Network Framework (v3)
summary: Describes Storj's decentralized cloud object storage with erasure-coded data across independent storage nodes and satellite coordination.

title: CryptoNote v2.0
summary: Introduces untraceable payments with ring signatures and unlinkable one-time addresses, the foundation for Monero.

title: Ring Confidential Transactions
summary: Combines ring signatures with confidential transactions so Monero can hide amounts as well as senders.

title: Zerocash: Decentralized Anonymous Payments from Bitcoin
authors: Eli Ben-Sasson, Alessandro Chiesa, Christina Garman, Matthew Green, Ian Miers, Eran Tromer, Madars Virza
summary: Proposes a decentralized anonymous payment scheme using zk-SNARKs that hides payment origin, destination and amount; the basis of Zcash.

title: Zcash Protocol Specification
authors: Daira-Emma Hopwood, Sean Bowe, Taylor Hornby, Nathan Wilcox
summary: The living specification of the Zcash protocol, covering the Sprout, Sapling and Orchard shielded pools and their zk-SNARK circuits.

title: Mimblewimble
summary: Formalizes Mimblewimble, a design with confidential amounts and cut-through that lets the chain be compacted while hiding transaction graphs.

title: Bulletproofs: Short Proofs for Confidential Transactions and More
authors: Benedikt Bünz, Jonathan Bootle, Dan Boneh, Andrew Poelstra, Pieter Wuille, Greg Maxwell
summary: Short non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs without a trusted setup, used for range proofs in confidential transactions such as Monero's.

title: Scalable, Transparent, and Post-Quantum Secure Computational Integrity (STARKs)
authors: Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh, Michael Riabzev
summary: Introduces zk-STARKs, transparent proof systems with no trusted setup and post-quantum security, which power StarkWare's scaling products.

title: On the Size of Pairing-based Non-interactive Arguments (Groth16)
summary: A pairing-based zk-SNARK with proofs of just three group elements, widely used in Zcash and many ZK applications.

title: PLONK: Permutations over Lagrange-bases for Oecumenical Noninteractive arguments of Knowledge
authors: Ariel Gabizon, Zachary J. Williamson, Oana Ciobotaru
summary: A universal and updatable zk-SNARK with a single trusted setup for all circuits, the basis of many modern ZK rollups.

title: Solana Alpenglow Consensus (v1.1)
authors: Quentin Kniep, Jakub Sliwinski, Roger Wattenhofer
summary: Alpenglow is a new consensus protocol for Solana, pairing the Votor voting protocol with Rotor data dissemination, aiming for finality in about 100 to 150 ms.

title: Jito: JitoSOL and MEV on Solana (Docs)
summary: Jito has no whitepaper; its docs describe JitoSOL, a liquid staking token earning staking plus MEV rewards from Jito's block-engine auctions, governed by JTO.

title: Jupiter Green Paper (Archived)
summary: Jupiter's founding strategy document, covering its role as Solana's liquidity aggregator, the JUP token, the DAO and Jupiter's launchpad.

title: Raydium RAY Token White Paper (Docs)
summary: Raydium's white paper page describing its Solana AMM, originally integrated with Serum's central limit order book, and the RAY token.

title: Helium: A Decentralized Wireless Network
authors: Amir Haleem, Andrew Allen, Andrew Thompson, Marc Nijdam, Rahul Garg
summary: Proposes a decentralized wireless network for IoT where hotspot owners earn tokens for coverage verified by Proof-of-Coverage. Helium migrated to Solana in 2023.

title: Render Network Whitepaper
summary: Describes a decentralized GPU rendering and compute marketplace connecting creators with node operators, settled in RENDER on Solana.

title: Bittensor: A Peer-to-Peer Intelligence Market
summary: Proposes a market where machine-learning models rank one another's value and are rewarded in TAO through a collusion-resistant incentive mechanism.

title: Livepeer Whitepaper
summary: Describes a decentralized live-video transcoding network where staked LPT holders coordinate work and verify transcoders.
